# Software Engineer - Backend
Location: Arlington, VA

Software Engineer - Backend

Job Description:

We are seeking a highly independent and proactive Software Engineer to join our backend team and play a critical role in building REST API microservices from scratch using ASP.NET Core (C#) and building cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) in AWS. In this role, you will contribute to collaborative file redacting tool with exciting features like live editing, image processing and more

What you will do:

- Model business domains into relational/NoSQL data structures

- Design and build scalable REST APIs for our microservices using ASP.NET Core (C#).

- Build heavy file-processing workers optimized for CPU/memory/throughput

- Design AWS infrastructure with IaC

- Participate in architectural discussions and contribute to decisions for system design and service structure.

Qualifications (Required):

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent experiences

- 2+ years backend experience with REST APIs

- Strong OOP fundamentals and critical thinking under ambiguity

- Experience with relational databases and SQL, including schema design, indexes, and transactions. 

- Experience with Redis or distributed caching. 

- A track record of modeling business logic into databases

- Comfort working independently on complex, underspecified problems

Qualifications (It’s a plus):

- Strong understanding of distributed systems, scalability, and fault-tolerance patterns.

- Familiarity with API design patterns such as Clean Architecture.

- Experience processing PDFs, images, videos, or other large binary files. 

- Hands-on experience with AWS services (e.g., EC2, EKS, S3, Lambda, RDS, DynamoDB).

- Practical knowledge of IaC tools (e.g., AWS CDK, Terraform, CloudFormation).

- Experience with containerization tools (e.g., Docker) and orchestration platforms (e.g., Kubernetes).

- Familiarity with event-driven architectures and message queues (e.g., SNS, SQS, EventBridge).

- Knowledge of asynchronous programming and multi-threading in C#.

- Relevant AWS certifications (e.g., AWS Certified Solutions Architect, AWS Certified Developer)

Benefits:

- Competitive Salary

- Stock Option

- Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance

- 401K

- Paid Vacation

- Ten paid holidays per year

- Friendly and Learning environment

About CaseGuard

CaseGuard is a software company that helps law enforcement agencies, federal agencies, hospitals, schools, airports, and others manage all their media redaction needs in one easy-to-use redaction software. CaseGuard Studio is one of a kind. Our team is driven by a passion for great software design, creating great products, and creative processes; CaseGuard implements innovative ideas across multiple services and agencies. We invest in people. We nurture skills consistent with our values and our future strategy. Our passionate pursuit of excellence, the application of our creativity to solve our clients’ challenges, our technical expertise, and our collaborative spirit are measures of our success.

final_report:
# CaseGuard: Interview Briefing

CaseGuard is a small, Arlington, VA-based data security company (founded in 2014) that builds CaseGuard Studio, an on-premise AI redaction platform used by law enforcement, government agencies, and other regulated organizations to redact sensitive information from video, audio, documents, and images. This backend role sits at the center of that mission: building REST API microservices in ASP.NET Core, standing up AWS infrastructure via IaC, and building heavy file-processing workers for the product's redaction and media-processing features. Below is a briefing pulling together what's known and reported about the company to help you prepare.

## Role Context
- CaseGuard Studio is marketed as an on-premise AI redaction platform covering video, audio, documents, and images from a single interface, though a specific figure of 33 categories of PII/PCI/PHI cited in one source appears inconsistent with the company's own materials elsewhere, so that exact number shouldn't be taken as confirmed. ([source](https://caseguard.com/how-it-works))
- CaseGuard reportedly positions the Studio as helping organizations meet FOIA, FERPA, GDPR, and HIPAA requirements while keeping sensitive files off the cloud, according to the company's own site, though this hasn't been independently verified. ([source](https://caseguard.com/how-it-works))
- CaseGuard's AI redaction software supports over 750 file types and formats, including video, audio, images, documents, and emails. ([source](https://caseguard.com/bulk-redaction-software))
- According to CaseGuard's own materials, its bulk redaction tools let users upload and process multiple video, audio, and image files simultaneously across 12 categories of PII, though that specific category count hasn't been independently confirmed. ([source](https://caseguard.com/bulk-redaction-software))
- The company claims its bulk AI redaction can clear case backlogs up to 85% faster, cutting review time from days to hours — a statistic repeated across several CaseGuard pages but not independently verified. ([source](https://caseguard.com/help-center/videos/caseguard-studio-training-course))
- Per a legal-tech directory listing, CaseGuard Studio can reportedly operate both online and fully offline, which the company positions as useful for legal teams and law enforcement facing strict data-privacy requirements, though this hasn't been independently confirmed. ([source](https://directory.lawnext.com/products/caseguard-studio))
- CaseGuard, Inc. was founded in 2014. ([source](https://directory.lawnext.com/products/caseguard-studio))

## Recent News
- One dedicated news article on CaseGuard Studio's privacy positioning reports that the platform runs fully on-premise, including in air-gapped systems completely isolated from external networks, so organizations retain full control of their data — though the specifics of this air-gapped isolation haven't been independently confirmed. ([source](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/ai-redaction-that-puts-privacy-first-caseguard-studio-leading-the-way))
- CaseGuard reportedly has shipped iterative product updates, including version releases 9.7, 9.8, and 9.9 with new feature drops, according to its video library, though these specific version numbers haven't been independently verified. ([source](https://caseguard.com/video-library))

## Funding & Business
- CaseGuard's estimated revenue reached about $4.1M as of September 2025, with no publicly reported funding rounds. ([source](https://getlatka.com/companies/caseguard.com))
- CaseGuard has approximately 57 employees (48 per RocketReach data) and reported revenue of about $6 million, though other sources give somewhat lower figures. ([source](https://rocketreach.co/caseguard-profile_b452b0abfc8d6e63))

## Tech Stack
- According to one interview-prep guide, Software Engineers at CaseGuard should be familiar with technologies including C#, ASP.NET Core, AWS, WebAssembly, WebGL, and modern frontend frameworks for building high-performance media processing applications — though the WebAssembly/WebGL specifics go beyond what's in the job posting and haven't been independently confirmed. ([source](https://www.interviewquery.com/interview-guides/caseguard-software-engineer))
- CaseGuard reportedly offers unlimited automated redaction of faces, license plates, screens, and notes in videos and images, plus muting, bleeping, or replacing PII in audio via auto-transcription, per a legal-tech directory listing that hasn't been independently verified. ([source](https://directory.lawnext.com/products/caseguard-studio))
- CaseGuard's Redaction Studio is said to support bulk redaction of over 100 videos at once using AI, according to the company's video library, though this figure hasn't been independently confirmed. ([source](https://caseguard.com/video-library))
- CaseGuard reportedly allows analysis of up to 16 videos side-by-side for faster investigations, per its video library page, though this hasn't been independently verified. ([source](https://caseguard.com/video-library))
- CaseGuard's bulk redaction feature is described as able to automatically redact thousands of videos, documents, audio, and image files simultaneously in just a few clicks, according to a company use-case page, though this hasn't been independently confirmed. ([source](https://caseguard.com/use-cases/media-and-entertainment))

## Culture
- CaseGuard is a data security software company based in Arlington, Virginia, with 11 to 50 employees, headquartered at 1700 North Moore Street, Arlington, VA 22209. ([source](https://leadiq.com/c/caseguard/6446f49f7aa418315617eb20/employee-directory))
- CaseGuard reportedly has a Talent Acquisition Specialist on staff, suggesting an active hiring function, though this specific role detail hasn't been independently verified. ([source](https://rocketreach.co/caseguard-profile_b452b0abfc8d6e63))

## Talking Points
1. CaseGuard's emphasis on heavy file-processing performance (e.g., claims of clearing backlogs up to 85% faster) lines up well with the role's focus on building CPU/memory/throughput-optimized file-processing workers — worth highlighting any prior experience optimizing large binary file pipelines.
2. CaseGuard Studio's on-premise, reportedly air-gapped deployment model and compliance focus (FOIA, FERPA, GDPR, HIPAA) suggest the backend team needs engineers comfortable designing secure, self-hosted AWS infrastructure with IaC — a good moment to speak to any experience with regulated or isolated environments.
3. As a lean team (roughly 11-50 employees, single-digit-million revenue) building microservices from scratch, CaseGuard likely needs someone who thrives on ambiguity and ownership — a strong match if you can point to independent work modeling business logic into databases and designing APIs end-to-end.
4. Given the product's scale claims around bulk processing (thousands of files, 100+ videos at once), the candidate's experience with relational/NoSQL data modeling and Redis or distributed caching directly supports the kind of throughput CaseGuard's redaction pipeline seems to require.
5. With reported iterative releases (9.7-9.9) and an active hiring function, CaseGuard appears to be scaling its engineering output — a chance to express interest in joining a growing team that ships frequent feature updates to its redaction platform.

## Questions to Ask Them
- Given CaseGuard Studio's on-premise and reportedly air-gapped deployment model, how does the backend team approach AWS infrastructure and IaC design when many customer environments may be isolated from the cloud?
- What does the current microservice architecture look like today, and how much of the AWS/backend build-out for this role would be greenfield versus extending existing services?
- For the heavy file-processing workers handling video, image, and document redaction, what are the current bottlenecks in CPU, memory, or throughput, and what patterns (e.g., queues, distributed caching, async processing) is the team exploring?
- How does the team balance frequent feature releases with maintaining fault tolerance and scalability as the customer base and file volumes grow?
- What does day-to-day collaboration look like between the backend team and other functions, given the company's relatively small engineering team?

briefing.intro: CaseGuard is a small, Arlington, VA-based data security company (founded in 2014) that builds CaseGuard Studio, an on-premise AI redaction platform used by law enforcement, government agencies, and other regulated organizations to redact sensitive information from video, audio, documents, and images. This backend role sits at the center of that mission: building REST API microservices in ASP.NET Core, standing up AWS infrastructure via IaC, and building heavy file-processing workers for the product's redaction and media-processing features. Below is a briefing pulling together what's known and reported about the company to help you prepare.

points.text: CaseGuard Studio is marketed as an on-premise AI redaction platform covering video, audio, documents, and images from a single interface, though a specific figure of 33 categories of PII/PCI/PHI cited in one source appears inconsistent with the company's own materials elsewhere, so that exact number shouldn't be taken as confirmed.

CaseGuard reportedly positions the Studio as helping organizations meet FOIA, FERPA, GDPR, and HIPAA requirements while keeping sensitive files off the cloud, according to the company's own site, though this hasn't been independently verified.
CaseGuard's AI redaction software supports over 750 file types and formats, including video, audio, images, documents, and emails.

According to CaseGuard's own materials, its bulk redaction tools let users upload and process multiple video, audio, and image files simultaneously across 12 categories of PII, though that specific category count hasn't been independently confirmed.

The company claims its bulk AI redaction can clear case backlogs up to 85% faster, cutting review time from days to hours — a statistic repeated across several CaseGuard pages but not independently verified.

Per a legal-tech directory listing, CaseGuard Studio can reportedly operate both online and fully offline, which the company positions as useful for legal teams and law enforcement facing strict data-privacy requirements, though this hasn't been independently confirmed.

One dedicated news article on CaseGuard Studio's privacy positioning reports that the platform runs fully on-premise, including in air-gapped systems completely isolated from external networks, so organizations retain full control of their data — though the specifics of this air-gapped isolation haven't been independently confirmed.

CaseGuard reportedly has shipped iterative product updates, including version releases 9.7, 9.8, and 9.9 with new feature drops, according to its video library, though these specific version numbers haven't been independently verified.
CaseGuard's estimated revenue reached about $4.1M as of September 2025, with no publicly reported funding rounds.
CaseGuard has approximately 57 employees (48 per RocketReach data) and reported revenue of about $6 million, though other sources give somewhat lower figures.

According to one interview-prep guide, Software Engineers at CaseGuard should be familiar with technologies including C#, ASP.NET Core, AWS, WebAssembly, WebGL, and modern frontend frameworks for building high-performance media processing applications — though the WebAssembly/WebGL specifics go beyond what's in the job posting and haven't been independently confirmed.

CaseGuard reportedly offers unlimited automated redaction of faces, license plates, screens, and notes in videos and images, plus muting, bleeping, or replacing PII in audio via auto-transcription, per a legal-tech directory listing that hasn't been independently verified.
CaseGuard's Redaction Studio is said to support bulk redaction of over 100 videos at once using AI, according to the company's video library, though this figure hasn't been independently confirmed.
CaseGuard reportedly allows analysis of up to 16 videos side-by-side for faster investigations, per its video library page, though this hasn't been independently verified.

CaseGuard's bulk redaction feature is described as able to automatically redact thousands of videos, documents, audio, and image files simultaneously in just a few clicks, according to a company use-case page, though this hasn't been independently confirmed.
CaseGuard is a data security software company based in Arlington, Virginia, with 11 to 50 employees, headquartered at 1700 North Moore Street, Arlington, VA 22209.
CaseGuard reportedly has a Talent Acquisition Specialist on staff, suggesting an active hiring function, though this specific role detail hasn't been independently verified.

talking_points: CaseGuard's emphasis on heavy file-processing performance (e.g., claims of clearing backlogs up to 85% faster) lines up well with the role's focus on building CPU/memory/throughput-optimized file-processing workers — worth highlighting any prior experience optimizing large binary file pipelines.

CaseGuard Studio's on-premise, reportedly air-gapped deployment model and compliance focus (FOIA, FERPA, GDPR, HIPAA) suggest the backend team needs engineers comfortable designing secure, self-hosted AWS infrastructure with IaC — a good moment to speak to any experience with regulated or isolated environments.

As a lean team (roughly 11-50 employees, single-digit-million revenue) building microservices from scratch, CaseGuard likely needs someone who thrives on ambiguity and ownership — a strong match if you can point to independent work modeling business logic into databases and designing APIs end-to-end.

Given the product's scale claims around bulk processing (thousands of files, 100+ videos at once), the candidate's experience with relational/NoSQL data modeling and Redis or distributed caching directly supports the kind of throughput CaseGuard's redaction pipeline seems to require.

With reported iterative releases (9.7-9.9) and an active hiring function, CaseGuard appears to be scaling its engineering output — a chance to express interest in joining a growing team that ships frequent feature updates to its redaction platform.
questions_to_ask: Given CaseGuard Studio's on-premise and reportedly air-gapped deployment model, how does the backend team approach AWS infrastructure and IaC design when many customer environments may be isolated from the cloud?
What does the current microservice architecture look like today, and how much of the AWS/backend build-out for this role would be greenfield versus extending existing services?

For the heavy file-processing workers handling video, image, and document redaction, what are the current bottlenecks in CPU, memory, or throughput, and what patterns (e.g., queues, distributed caching, async processing) is the team exploring?
How does the team balance frequent feature releases with maintaining fault tolerance and scalability as the customer base and file volumes grow?
What does day-to-day collaboration look like between the backend team and other functions, given the company's relatively small engineering team?
